newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire Elec agrees to U.S. takeover - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire Elec agrees to U.S. takeover - paper.

text.p: Yorkshire Electricity is set to announce it has agreed to a 1.5 billion stg ($2.43 billion) takeover by American Electric Powers and another unnamed U.S. power group, the Daily Telegraph said on Monday.
The newspaper said the Yorkshire board had clinched a price of 900 pence per share, up from the initial offer of 860 pence per share.
The deal was agreed in talks held at the the offices of merchant bank NM Rothschild which was Yorkshire's adviser, said the Telegraph.
The Financial Times on Monday echoed weekend reports which said Yorkshire was poised for a takeover bid of up to 1.5 billion.
The newspaper said American Electric Powers (AEP), of Ohio, was involved in talks late on Sunday night.
Yorkshire and Southern Electric are the only independent regional electricity companies left out of the original 12 British privatised firms.
AEP is one of the biggest electricity companies in the U.S. and capitalised at 4.8 billion stg.
